newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam ousts disgraced politician from assembly.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam ousts disgraced politician from assembly.

text.p: A senior politician, expelled from Vietnam's Politburo earlier this year amid allegations of treason, has been ousted as deputy chairman of the National Assembly, Voice of Vietnam radio said on Thursday.
"The National Assembly officially dismissed Mr Nguyen Ha Phan as deputy chairman ... at its meeting this morning," Voice of Vietnam said.
Once a rising star within the Politburo, Phan was stripped of party membership as a punishment for making "a serious mistake in past activities".
The radio gave no reason for his dismissal from the National Assembly, the lawmaking body.
Informed sources say Phan, 63, was accused of passing information about communist guerrilas to the U.S.-backed South Vietnam police in the late 1950s.
He is also accused of securing his own release from detention during the Vietnam War almost a decade later by promising to collaborate with the Americans.
The sources said the trigger for Phan's troubles came early this year when fingers were pointed at him over the leaking of an internal document.

Phan, who was secretary of the party's Central Committee as well as deputy chairman of the National Assembly, had previously been seen as a possible contender to replace Vo Van Kiet as prime minister.
He was placed under house arrest after the affair blew up. Details of his current whereabouts are unclear and it was not possible to contact him.
Phan was a close ally of another senior Politburo member, Dao Duy Tung, who disappeared from the political scene shortly before the mid-year party congress after he became seriously ill.
